scenes.text: A burger covered in gold. A truffle that once sold for over three hundred thousand dollars. A dessert that comes with diamonds. And it's all one dinner.
Welcome to Billionaire Bites. Our vision is simple: to take you inside the world's most extraordinary food, where every dish is jewelry on a plate, and every price has a story.
Tonight, one table in a dark dining room is set for a single guest. His order to the chef was simple: cook me the most expensive dinner on Earth.
The chef has one night, and a menu of five courses. Every ingredient must come from the best place in the world. So the journey begins.
Course one begins in a field at dawn. One gram of saffron takes about one hundred and fifty flowers.
Each flower blooms for only a few days a year, and holds just three crimson threads. Every thread is picked by hand, before the sun can fade it.
The threads are slowly dried, until deep red turns to liquid gold. Did you already know? That is why saffron is the most expensive spice on Earth.
Back in the kitchen, the chef soaks the threads in warm milk. Good to know: this releases the color and flavor, so a pinch can paint a whole pot of rice.
The first plate reaches the table, golden and fragrant. One course down. Now the chef needs something from the forest.
Course two begins at night, in an Italian forest near Alba. Hunters rely on trained dogs to sniff out the white truffle, hidden among tree roots.
Nobody has ever farmed it reliably. This ugly lump of dirt can cost more than gold, and its aroma fades within days.
Did you already know? One giant white truffle once sold for over three hundred thousand dollars.
So the truffle races to the kitchen, and is shaved fresh over a warm plate. Good to know: truffles are never really cooked. The heat of the dish is enough to wake up the aroma.
Course three comes from Japan. Real Kobe beef comes only from Hyogo, and every cut is tracked from farm to plate.
It's A5 wagyu, the highest grade of beef on Earth. Inspectors score the marbling, those white ribbons of fat, from one to twelve.
In the pan, the fat melts at a lower temperature than normal beef, so it dissolves on your tongue. Good to know: a few thin slices are enough.
One steak can cost hundreds of dollars. The plate is set before the guest, but the chef is saving the boldest idea for course four.
Course four is a surprise. The chef takes that wagyu and builds a burger, a thick patty seared until the fat glistens, on a toasted brioche bun.
Next comes a spoonful of caviar, the salted eggs of the sturgeon fish. The rarest comes from an albino sturgeon, and can cost tens of thousands of dollars a kilo.
The finishing touch is real, edible, twenty four karat gold leaf. Did you already know? It is so thin, it is completely edible.
Good to know: gold has no taste. It simply passes through your body. You are paying for the look, and the story. Some of these burgers sell for more than a thousand dollars.
Before dessert, the chef serves a palate cleanser, with vanilla. Every orchid flower opens for just one day, so farmers pollinate each one by hand.
And edible bird's nest, made from the dried saliva of swiftlets, prized in Chinese cooking for centuries.
Notice the pattern. Hand picking, hand pollinating, hand harvesting. Luxury food is usually expensive because of human time, not just rare ingredients.
Now the final course. The chef turns to the most famous luxury dessert in the world. It was served at Serendipity 3 in New York for twenty five thousand dollars, and it set a Guinness record.
The goblet is lined with edible gold, and it sits on an eighteen karat gold bracelet with diamonds.
You eat it with a gold spoon set with diamonds, and you get to keep it.
Five courses. A spice from a flower field, a truffle from a forest, beef from Japan, a burger crowned in caviar and gold, and a dessert that doubles as jewelry.
The candle burns low. The table is empty, and the guest is gone. All that is left is the story of where every bite came from.
Now it's your turn. If you could only pick one course from tonight's menu, which would it be? Tell us in the comments.
Follow Billionaire Bites for more jewelry on a plate. Next time, we'll find an even more expensive menu.
